record.original_question: Let Ω be a simply connected open subset of R^n with the following two-convexity property: whenever three faces of a Euclidean 3-simplex Δ lie in Ω, the whole simplex Δ lies in Ω. Is every connected component of the intersection of Ω with an arbitrary 2-dimensional affine plane necessarily simply connected?

evidence.quote: Let Ω be a simply connected open set in R^n. Assume that Ω is two-convex; that is, if 3 faces of a 3-simplex △ lie in Ω, then △ ⊂ Ω. Is it true that any component of the intersection of Ω with any 2-plane is simply connected?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Call an open set Ω ⊂ ℝⁿ two-convex if, for every Euclidean 3-simplex Δ ⊂ ℝⁿ, the inclusion of three of its 2-dimensional faces in Ω forces Δ ⊂ Ω. Suppose Ω is a simply connected open subset of ℝⁿ that is two-convex in this sense. Must it then be true that, for every 2-dimensional affine plane P ⊂ ℝⁿ, every connected component of Ω ∩ P is simply connected?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is listed as an open question in a collection of geometric open problems. It is known to hold when the boundary of Ω is a smooth hypersurface (via a Morse/Lefschetz-type argument using that two-convexity bounds the number of negative principal curvatures) and when n = 3, but the general case for arbitrary two-convex simply connected open sets remains open.

status_evidence.title: A gallery of open problems in geometry
status_evidence.snippet: Let Ω be a simply connected open set in R^n. Assume that Ω is two-convex... Is it true that any component of the intersection of Ω with any 2-plane is simply connected? The answer is yes if the boundary is a smooth hypersurface, and also yes if n=3.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is posed as open in general; partial results hold for smooth boundary and for n=3.
